messages.content:
You are the single FlowLens agent reviewing an authorised test website end to end. You alone explore it, design input tests for forms you find, judge the outcomes, and choose the verification assertion for your own suspected defects. Code executes browser actions in fresh sessions and evaluates assertions. Your notes from earlier steps of this same review are included in every step.

Instructions for this step:
You are the Input Tester inside FlowLens, a website reviewer. An explorer found a form on an authorised test website and handed it to you with the supplied requirements.

Design a small set of input cases that check what the requirements say about this form: include boundary and invalid values the requirements address, plus at least one valid control case. Code will enter each case in a fresh browser session, submit it, and record what the page does.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"reasoning": "<one sentence>", "cases": [
  {"label": "<short name>", "inputs": {"<field name exactly as listed>": "<value>"},
   "submit": "<submit control name exactly as listed>",
   "requirement_ref": "<requirement id this case checks, or null>",
   "expected": "<what should happen, according to that requirement>",
   "check_page": "<optional: a page path from 'Links' where the effect should be visible, or null>"}]}

Rules:
- Use only the field and submit names listed. Unlisted fields keep their current value.
- A form with no fields performs an action (confirm, delete, cancel ...). Use "inputs": {} for it.
- If a requirement says the action changes another page (for example, an item disappears from a list),
  set check_page to that page's path. Code opens it in the same session before and after the action.
- Values are typed exactly. A field with type=date needs YYYY-MM-DD.
- Set requirement_ref only when a supplied requirement states the expected behaviour. If none does, use null and describe your own expectation; it will be treated as a review observation, not a defect.
- At most 3 cases. Keep labels and expectations to one short line each.
- Reply with compact JSON on a single line (no indentation).

Your notes from earlier in this review:
[explore] { "reasoning": "I will start by opening the booking form for the first event listed to satisfy the goal of exploring available forms.", "action": { "type": "click", "element_id": "e2" } }
[explore] { "reasoning": "I have opened the booking form for the first event. Now I will return to the events list to see if there are other events or forms to explore.", "action": { "type": "click", "element_id": "e1" } }
[explore] { "reasoning": "I have already explored the booking form for the first event. Now I will open the booking form for the second event, 'Open-Air Cinema', to ensure all available forms are explored.", "action": { "type": "click", "element_id": "e3" } }
[explore] { "reasoning": "I have explored the booking forms for both events listed on the home page. I will now return to the home page to check if there are any other links or forms I missed.", "action": { "type": "click", "element_id": "e1" } }
[explore] { "reasoning": "I have explored the booking forms for all listed events and checked the 'My bookings' section, which currently has no forms. I have completed the exploration of available forms.", "action": { "type": "finish", "persistence": "unknown", "checked

Supplied requirements:
- T1: A visitor can open the booking form for an event from the events list.
- T2: A booking must be for between 1 and 6 tickets. Any other number must be rejected with a validation message, and no booking is created.
- T3: The email must contain an "@". Otherwise the booking is rejected with a validation message.
- T4: After a successful booking, a confirmation page shows the event, the name and the number of tickets.
- T5: A booking can be cancelled from its confirmation page after confirming. A cancelled booking no longer appears under My bookings.

Form handed over by single-agent:
Page: http://localhost:5176/events/1/book
Headings: Book tickets
Fields:
  - "Name" (textbox, type=text)
  - "Email" (textbox, type=text)
  - "Tickets" (textbox, type=number)
Submit controls: "Book tickets"
Links on this page: /
Visible page text (truncated): Ticket Desk · Events Book tickets Harbour Jazz Night Name Email Tickets Book tickets

response: {"reasoning": "I will test the ticket quantity boundaries and email format requirements to ensure proper validation and successful booking.", "cases": [{"label": "Valid booking", "inputs": {"Name": "Alice", "Email": "alice@example.com", "Tickets": "2"}, "submit": "Book tickets", "requirement_ref": "T4", "expected": "Confirmation page shows event, name, and 2 tickets."}, {"label": "Invalid tickets (high)", "inputs": {"Name": "Bob", "Email": "bob@example.com", "Tickets": "7"}, "submit": "Book tickets", "requirement_ref": "T2", "expected": "Validation message appears and no booking is created."}, {"label": "Invalid email", "inputs": {"Name": "Charlie", "Email": "charlie-at-example.com", "Tickets": "1"}, "submit": "Book tickets", "requirement_ref": "T3", "expected": "Validation message appears and booking is rejected."}]}
